mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE increases by >0.3pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and high payroll employment indicate a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE is low and PAYEMS is high, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production indicates strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate combined with rising CPI indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS is high and CPIAUCSL is rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales indicate high consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when RSAFS > $700,000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rapidly increasing payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS increases rapidly, the hypothesis is rejected.
